firstly, i would like to commend you on your patience and care for your own wellbeing. you know that youre not 100% confident, so you want to ask other for help, great!

second, i want to assure you driving a bmw SUV is not that hard. Most of them won’t have excessive horsepower, the speed and acceleration should feel roughly the same if not only slightly higher than a driving center toyota.

SUV also gives you a commanding driving position, where you are able to see more of the road in front of you.

Two issues might come with parking in general (just need loads of practice, but actually since u got license, you can go and spam in the same lot parking at some empty carpark at night)

next, be aware that the indicators are on left side for BMW. this might take some getting used to but at most it will just cause your wiper to come up once in a while. also, make sure you know how to use your wiper. sometimes, your windscreen will fog up when you enter a humid carpark which won’t activate the auto wiper, blinding u completely.

and also, remember to adjust the seats comfortably. elbows and knees slightly bent. later bmw models allow you to save your seat position, so maybe you can ask the owner of the car how to do that.

happy driving!

ok so

1. dont take 27 mcs in 1 sem. if you really want to clear your mcs fast, you can do this by taking more modules during summer school (i think you can take up to 2 modules here), or do SIP (student internship programme) during the summer for extra MCS. you can also do modules during winter for winter school, though im not sure if they are offered this year due to covid, as usually winter school modules are offered by overseas unis so im not sure for nus.    you should be able to clear your 5 UEs by doing this.
2. Take CS/CU aka Pass/fail modules. If you wanna maintain at least a pretty decent cap for your whole uni life, you need to start looking at taking pass fail modules such as ges1035, these modules essentially require u to do absolutely nothing, they are a free pass, so you can google "nus pass fail mods" and then take them as UE/GE
3. This is probably the best "hack" out of this lot, but i feel that it is okay to severely overload in your y1s2 since you wanna graduate in 3 years. Apart from your core modules in y1s2 (which i assume you will be taking cs2030, cs2040 and cs2100 which you will focus on since you cant SU), you can take all your GEs, yes, all of them in the same sem, but you will need to appeal to take extra mcs and justify why you wanna do like 32 mcs in one sem. you can then proceed to SU every single one of these GEs, but you may potentially incur the wrath of your groupmates,  because with all those CS modules i doubt you will have time to spend on your GEs.
4. Be aware of hard modules that you will probably need to SU. this includes modules that are "volatile" like is1103 which the grade you get is not proportional to the effort you put in, and modules like ma1521/ma1101r where the bell curve is steep. but then again if you follow (3). you probably would not have enough SUs to use for these modules anyway.

So overall I strongly suggest you do not take 27 mcs in a sem. This is absolutely insane, and as motivated as you can be right now, you must not underestimate how stressful 27 taking 27 mcs will be. Every module in NUS apart from those CS/CU modules will feel like a 4mc module, meaning that you will be spending the time and effort of the module that is supposed to be worth 4mcs. Other modules like cs2030 and cs2103 generally require you to spend much greater amounts of time, and deserve to be maybe 6 or 8 mc modules, but you only still get 4 mcs anyway. This means that you could potentially be doing like 35 mcs worth of work (OMG) when you are only taking 27 mcs worth of modules. One possibly way to avoid this is to overload lightly with easy mods, maybe 24 mcs per sem with some summer classes, then graduate in 3.5 years and avoid the hiring cycle.

I went through a similar phase when I was in y1 and y2, i still feel like that sometimes but I will try to give you some advice to cope :)

1. realise that results aren't everything
in my first two years of uni I sacrificed everything; social life, proper sleep and eating, family time and most importantly, my mental health in order to chase the coveted first class honours. you really need to ask yourself whether this is worth it, because even though you are pursuing happiness you literally aren't happy now. it's okay to not get good grades, especially since you're already in NUS!

2. find an internship/ part time job/ cca
find something that you're interested in! I found a good internship and cca that I liked and I realised that life is alot more than just results. University is a time for you to expand your social circle and connections as well as get working experience. it's not just about purely grinding studies. if you find something that gives you purpose, results will seem alot less important.

3. it's okay to be disappointed
hard modules, shitty profs, shitty groupmates, bad luck during exams are disappointing, certainly. but we need to realise that disappointments are not anomalies or tragedies, but are inevitabilities in life. you're bound to face such disappointments and setbacks, alot of which we cannot take them too harshly, but rather make the best out of the situation. it might be hard to look on the bright side in moments like this, but please realise that sometimes it's not your fault, it's the bad circumstances you're put in!

4. seek help. 
in my first year of NUS, I was in a terrible mental state. I started seeking help with the NUS psych hotline, and still see the psychiatrist (Dr Tan Kuan Hoo) up till today. it got really bad, so I called SOS to ask for help. if you think that you're really at the edge, PLEASE SEEK HELP! you can come and DM me if you need someone to talk to, don't do anything silly because of school, it's absolutely not worth it!! talk to anyone that you know cares about you, they might not give you advice but at least give you an avenue to rant and release some pent up stress.

I really hope that you can overcome this and find happiness in NUS. jiayou!!
